summary: Johan Nicolai Madvig worked in linguistics. He studied at Frederiksborg Gymnasium og HF (~1817–1820) and the University of Copenhagen (~1820–1826), where he later held an academic post from circa 1829 to 1879.

Johan van Manen was a scholar of Tibetology and Indology. He served as second Librarian at Adyar Library (1909–1916), Librarian at the National Library of India (1918–1921), and General Secretary of The Asiatic Society (1923–1939).

Johann Albrecht Bernhard von Dorn studied at Halle-Wittenberg and Leipzig. A scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and Indology, he held posts at the University of Kharkiv, Saint Petersburg Academy of Sciences, and as director of the Asiatic Museum.

Johann Andreas Schmeller studied at the University of Munich (~1801–1803). He taught at the Bavarian Cadet Corps (~1814–1826) and served at the Bavarian State Library from 1829, also holding professorial posts at the University of Munich from 1828 and 1846.

Johann August Vullers was a scholar of linguistics and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied at Giessen, Bonn, and Halle-Wittenberg under teachers including Schlegel, Silvestre de Sacy, and Bopp. He held posts at Bonn (1831) and Giessen (1833).
Johann Caspar von Orelli was a linguistics scholar. He held teaching posts at Bündner Kantonsschule (~1819–1831), Carolinum Zürich (~1831–1833), and the University of Zurich (~1833–1849).

Johann Christian Christoph Rüdiger worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg from 1768, where he later became a Privatdozent in 1777 and extraordinary professor of Kameralwissenschaften in 1791.

Johann Christoph Adelung worked in linguistics. He studied at Kloster Berge school (~1746–1752) and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (1752). He later served at Evangelisches Ratsgymnasium Erfurt (1758) and as head librarian at Dresden (1787).

Johann Detloff Prochnow was a scholar in linguistics and Indology who studied at the University of Greifswald (1837–1840). He served as a missionary with the Church Mission Society from 1843 and became director at Gossner Evangelical Lutheran Church around 1858.

Johann Dietrich Ludwig de Vries worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Utrecht, Amsterdam, Lille, and Bonn under Caland, Schrijnen, Jacobi, and Kirfel. In 1923, he served as deputy Professor of Latin at Stellenbosch University.

Johann Friedrich Blumenbach worked in history and archaeology. He studied at Ernestinum Gotha (~1765–1769), the University of Jena (~1769–1772), and the University of Göttingen (~1772–1775), where he later held a post from circa 1776 to 1840.
Johann Friedrich Herbart was a philosopher. He studied at the University of Jena (~1794–1797) and held a post at the University of Göttingen from circa 1802 to 1809.

Johann Friedrich Kleuker worked in religious studies and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Göttingen in 1770 and was appointed Professor of Theology at Kiel University in 1798.

Johann Gildemeister worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Göttingen and Bonn under Heinrich Ewald, Georg Freytag, and Christian Lassen. He held professorships at the University of Marburg (1845; 1848–1858) and the University of Bonn (1844–1889).

Johann Gottfried Eichhorn worked in religious studies, history/archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at Göttingen (1770–1774) under Christian Gottlob Heyne. He served as Professor of Oriental Languages at Jena (1775) and Professor of Philosophy at Göttingen (1788).

Johann Gottfried Ludwig Kosegarten, a scholar of Indology and linguistics, studied at Greifswald and in Paris under Silvestre de Sacy and Chézy. He was a professor at the University of Jena (1817–1824) and the University of Greifswald (1824–1850).

Johann Gottfried von Herder worked in philosophy, linguistics, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Königsberg under Immanuel Kant, later holding posts in Riga (1764–1769) and serving as director of Wilhelm-Ernst-Gymnasium Weimar (~1776–1803).

Johann Gottlieb Rhode worked in Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Helmstedt (~1782–1785) and the University of Jena (~1820–1821), and he taught at the Kriegsschule Berlin from 1809.

Johann Gustav Stickel was a linguistics scholar. He studied at the University of Jena (1823–1826) under Kosegarten and Hoffmann, and under Silvestre de Sacy (~1828–1830). He later served as a professor at the University of Jena (1830–1836).

Johann Heinrich Kalthoff worked in Indology. He studied at Münster, Bonn, and under Silvestre de Sacy and Abel-Rémusat. He served as Privatdozent at the University of Münster (1830–1839) and taught French at Gymnasium Paulinum (1831).
